statements.t: As a result of the Cullgen acquisition, we intend to leverage Cullgen’s capabilities in the PRC for the development and early-stage clinical trials of various product candidates.
F351 represents our primary liver-focused development program and reflects our commitment to advancing therapies targeting both viral- and metabolic-associated liver fibrosis.

We are now planning a Phase 2 study to further evaluate CG001419 in cancer-induced bone pain (CIBP) or other metastatic cancer pain syndromes in China, which is expected to initiate in the first half of 2027.
We anticipate Phase 1 dose-escalation data to be available in the second half of 2027.
We plan to develop CG923308 for the treatment of solid tumors with CCNE1 amplification or HR+ / HER2- advanced breast cancer with resistance to current therapies.
We intend to submit an IND application for CG923308 in the first quarter of 2027.
We intend to submit an IND application for CG620953 in the United States or China around mid-2027.
We are developing a robust suite of DACs that target both solid tumors and hematological malignancies by pairing distinct protein degraders with tumor-specific antibodies.

F230 complements our broader organ-focused portfolio by expanding our development efforts into pulmonary vascular disease while remaining aligned with our strategy of targeting fibrotic and inflammatory pathways across organ systems.
We anticipate submitting an IND application to the NMPA for F528 in 2026.

We manage our research and development expenses by identifying the research and development activities we expect to be performed during a given period and then prioritizing efforts based on anticipated probability of successful technical development and regulatory approval, market potential, available human and capital resources, scientific data and other considerations.

We regularly review our research and development activities based on unmet medical need and, as necessary, reallocate resources among our research and development portfolio that we believe will best support the long-term growth of our business.
We will continue to evaluate the impact of the OBBBA on our unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements.

We expect to use cash provided by operating activities, short-term deposits, and long-term certificates of deposit, as well as potential cash issuances to meet our current and future financial obligations, including funding our operations, research and development activities, clinical pipelines, and capital expenditures.
Our ability to make these payments depends on our future performance, which will be affected by financial, business, economic, regulatory, and other factors, many of which we cannot control.
In addition, we anticipate that we will incur expenses related to and in connection with the integration between our business and Cullgen.
our ability to manufacture sufficient quantities of our products to meet expected demand;

We expect to satisfy our contractual obligations and commitments through a combination of cash on hand, cash provided by operating activities, short-term deposits, and long-term certificates of deposit.

Our commitments related to the purchase of property and equipment contracted but not yet reflected in the unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements were $4.9 million as of September 30, 2026 and are expected to be incurred within one year.
